template_params.backend_side: signups and each subscription's first payment

prompt: Declan, the head of growth, wants the 2026 growth report to read sign-ups and first payments from the GA4 export instead of the backend, and asks whether the two agree for each first-touch source and medium over the Dublin days from 1 October to 31 December 2025. In events, event_date holds that Dublin day; signup_ts and paid_at hold UTC instants, so take their day in Europe/Dublin time. On the export side, a sign-up is a sign_up event and a first payment is a purchase event, and each such event counts once: the ones with no user_pseudo_id, from visitors who denied consent, count too, and so do the events Mailvora's server sends, every purchase among them. Their first touch is the source and medium in traffic_source, where direct traffic shows as (direct) and (none). On the backend side, a sign-up is a row of signups, dated by its signup_ts, and a first payment is each subscription's earliest payment, dated by its paid_at; a first payment that was later refunded still counts, as the export keeps its purchase. Their first touch is the utm_source and utm_medium of the visitor's first session, the one with the earliest session_start among all of the visitor's sessions, those before October included; a first payment's visitor is the visitor who signed up as the subscription's user, and a missing utm_source counts as (direct) and a missing utm_medium as (none). Return one row for each first-touch source and medium with at least one sign-up or first payment on either side, with six columns in this order: source; medium; ga4_signups and backend_signups, the sign-ups on each side; and ga4_first_payments and backend_first_payments, the first payments on each side. A count with nothing to count shows 0. Sort by source from A to Z, then by medium from A to Z.
hints: Next, count each side in its own step by first-touch source and medium: the export's sign_up and purchase events, then the backend's signups and each subscription's first payment.
On the backend side, take each visitor's earliest session over all of the visitor's sessions, and join the two sides so a source and medium found on one side only still gets a row.
why_this_works: Both sides count the same Dublin days and group by the same first touch, so a gap between two columns of a row would be a real difference, not a slip in the definition.
